title: FINALLY Block - Guaranteed Cleanup
description: Use FINALLY block to ensure cleanup code always runs, regardless of success or failure.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "When you open a connection, you MUST close it—even if errors occur. FINALLY guarantees cleanup code runs no matter what."
story.context: FINALLY is essential for resource cleanup: closing connections, releasing locks, saving logs. It runs whether TRY succeeds or fails.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Excellent! The connection attempt failed, but FINALLY still closed the port. No resource leaks. This is production-grade error handling."

hints: FINALLY comes AFTER EXCEPT (and ELSE if present)
FINALLY always runs - success or failure
Use for cleanup: closing files, connections, releasing resources
Order: TRY → EXCEPT → ELSE → FINALLY → END

solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Communication Port Test
    ${port_open}=    Set Variable    False
    TRY
        Log    Opening communication port 8080...
        ${port_open}=    Set Variable    True
        Log    Port opened
        Fail    Data transmission error
    EXCEPT    AS    ${error}
        Log    Communication error: ${error}
    FINALLY
        Log    Closing port (runs regardless of error)
        ${port_open}=    Set Variable    False
    END
    Log    Port status: ${port_open}

theory.title: Exercise 3.2.4: FINALLY - Guaranteed Cleanup
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Resources must be cleaned up—connections closed, locks released, files saved. FINALLY ensures cleanup happens even if errors occur. It's like a safety net for your cleanup code."

FINALLY Block - Always Executes

FINALLY runs regardless of success or failure:

TRY
    Open Resource
    Risky Operation
EXCEPT
    Handle Error
FINALLY
    Close Resource  # Always runs
END

Execution Scenarios:

  • Success: TRY → ELSE (if present) → FINALLY
  • Failure: TRY → EXCEPT → FINALLY
  • Both cases: FINALLY always executes

Example: Database Connection

${connected}=    Set Variable    False
TRY
    Log    Connecting to database...
    ${connected}=    Set Variable    True
    Log    Executing query...
    Fail    Query timeout  # Simulates error
EXCEPT    AS    ${err}
    Log    Database error: ${err}
FINALLY
    IF    ${connected}
        Log    Closing database connection
        ${connected}=    Set Variable    False
    END
END
Log    Connection status: ${connected}  # Will be False

Output: Even though query failed, FINALLY closed the connection. No resource leak.

⚠️ FINALLY Best Practices

  • Use for cleanup: close files, connections, release locks
  • FINALLY runs even if EXCEPT re-raises error
  • Order: TRY → EXCEPT → ELSE → FINALLY → END
  • Common pattern: open in TRY, close in FINALLY
  • Prevents resource leaks in long-running tests
  • Similar concept to teardown, but scoped to code block
